description: If you love space exploration, want to solve real astronaut health challenges, and want to build something impactful in a collaborative and supportive environment, hit "Join Team" or reach out to us! Let’s code for the stars with the blessing of Papa and Mama! ✨
summary: AstroVitals is an interactive, web-based health monitoring dashboard designed to empower astronauts on long-duration space missions. Addressing the critical challenge of deep-space communication delays, AstroVitals serves as an autonomous medical companion that allows crew members to track and evaluate their own physiological data without relying on real-time Earth support. The platform features an intuitive, clickable digital body map that displays real-time vitals (heart rate, oxygen, temperature, and blood glucose) and cross-references them with NASA's 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight. By aggregating daily health scores, integrating with wearable Bluetooth devices, and featuring a simulated Earth-link alerting system for critical health degradation, AstroVitals ensures that astronauts can proactively manage risks like cardiovascular changes, radiation exposure, and SANS before they become emergencies.
details:
What it does & How it works:

AstroVitals is a comprehensive crew dashboard that visualizes an astronaut's health status. Users interact with a digital body map to check specific systems. The app ingests data from paired Bluetooth health devices (like smartwatches, pulse oximeters, and chest straps) or uses simulated hardware inputs. It logs this data to generate historical trends and "Daily Scores."

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Because messages to Earth take time, astronauts must act as their own flight surgeons. AstroVitals reduces the cognitive load of medical tracking by using color-coded statuses (Good, Watch, Act) and automated medical reminders. Its intended impact is to increase crew autonomy, improve behavioral health, and prevent mission-critical medical failures.

Tools & Technologies:

The project was built using frontend web technologies—HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We utilized the Web Bluetooth API to allow real-time pairing with wearable hardware. The application is deployed seamlessly via GitHub Pages.

Creativity & Factors Considered:

Our team, DoaPaMa, focused heavily on the harsh realities of space physics and psychology. We creatively implemented a "Link to Earth" module that calculates real-time distance and communication delay (e.g., a 1.3-second one-way delay to the Moon). We also built an "Automatic Emergency Rule" engine: if a crew member hits a critical health score (under 65) for three consecutive days, the system simulates an automatic SOS packet drop to Mission Control. Every metric is closely aligned with NASA's Human Research Program and the CSA's radiation guidelines.
